title: Which altitudes of a right angled triangle are also sides?
description: In a triangle with a right angle at one corner, the two sides at that corner meet at ninety degrees. Each one is the perpendicular from the far corner, so each is an altitude. The third altitude falls inside. Keeko's doubt is that an altitude never lies on a side.
teaching_notes: One idea: in a triangle with a right angle, the two sides at the right angle are altitudes as well as sides. Watch for students who think an altitude has to be a new line drawn inside the triangle.

source: Does there exist a triangle in which a side is also an altitude? Visualise such a triangle and draw a rough diagram. We see that this happens in triangles where one of the angles is a right angle.
video_script.why: The child can draw an altitude inside a triangle and outside it, and now asks whether an altitude can be a side.
video_script.substitution: A triangle ABC with a right angle at B.
video_script.anchor: triangle ABC with a right angle at B
video_script.wrong_answer: an altitude never lies on a side
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko thinks an altitude is always a new line drawn inside the triangle, so it can never lie on a side, but a side that meets another side at a right angle is a perpendicular.
video_script.payoff_line: The sides eigh bee and bee cee are both altitudes

final_answer.value: AB and BC are both sides and altitudes in a right-angled triangle with the right angle at B
final_answer.spoken: the sides eigh bee and bee cee are both altitudes

maths_rules: ∠B = 90°, so AB is perpendicular to BC
the perpendicular from A to BC is AB itself, so AB is the altitude from A
the perpendicular from C to AB is BC itself, so BC is the altitude from C
the altitude from B goes to the long side AC and lies inside the triangle
video_script.design: The triangle with the right angle at B stays on the board. The two sides at B glow as altitudes in turn, and the third altitude is drawn from B to the long side as a dotted line.
